title: ISO 27001
summary: ISO/IEC 27001 is the international standard that specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an information security management system. It is a management-system standard rather than a control catalogue: it tells an organisation how to govern security through leadership commitment, documented scope, risk assessment, risk treatment, internal audit, management review and corrective action, while the accompanying guidance in ISO/IEC 27002 describes control objectives an organisation may select from. Certification is granted to the management system by an accredited certification body, not to a product, a data centre or a specific application, and it is issued against a declared scope and Statement of Applicability. For the security practitioner the practical consequences are concrete. Risk assessment must be repeatable and produce traceable treatment decisions; controls must be documented with owners, evidence and review cycles; Annex A control themes now cover organisational, people, physical and technological domains, and each selected or excluded control needs a justification. Auditors sample evidence rather than trust assertions, so operational artefacts such as access reviews, change tickets, incident records and supplier assessments become the real currency of the audit. Surveillance audits occur at least annually and a recertification audit happens on a three-year cycle, which means compliance is a continuous programme rather than a project with an end date. The standard pairs well with ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018 for cloud services and with ISO 27005 for risk methodology.
objectives: You will be able to explain how a risk assessment and risk treatment plan feed the Statement of Applicability and the audit programme.
You will be able to define an ISMS scope that matches the organisation's real legal, contractual and technical boundaries.
You will be able to map Annex A control themes onto existing operational controls and produce clause-level evidence.
You will be able to prepare for a stage 1 documentation review and a stage 2 evidence-based certification audit.
You will be able to run an internal audit and management review cycle that generates genuine corrective actions.
You will be able to identify the common failure modes where certification is achieved but security practice does not improve.

beginner.definition: ISO 27001 is an international standard for managing information security. ISO stands for the International Organization for Standardization, which publishes it. The standard does not list products to buy. Instead it describes how to build a management system: set the scope, assess risk, choose controls and keep improving. Certification covers that system.
beginner.whyItMatters: Customers and regulators often ask for proof that you manage security properly. Without a shared standard, every answer becomes a new questionnaire and a new argument. ISO 27001 gives you one agreed way to show how you decide what matters and how you check it works. It also creates steady habits instead of a yearly panic before an audit.
howItWorks: Define the scope: which teams, systems and locations the management system covers.
Assess the risks to information inside that scope and rank them clearly.
Choose controls that treat each risk, and write down why you chose them.
Record your decisions in policies, owners and evidence that auditors can check.
Run your own internal audits and management reviews on a regular schedule.
Fix what the reviews find, then repeat the cycle so the system improves.
beginner.example: Think of a restaurant kitchen with a food safety system. The kitchen does not just buy one good fridge. It sets rules, trains staff, records fridge temperatures, checks them and fixes problems. A health inspector then samples those records. ISO 27001 works the same way for information, and an auditor looks at your daily records rather than your promises.
takeaways: ISO 27001 certifies a management system, not a product or a building.
Risk assessment and written decisions are the core of the standard.
Auditors sample real records, so good daily habits matter more than documents.

exercises.title: ISO 27001 - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: ISO 27001 - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: ISO 27001 - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: ISO 27001 - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
